Testimony of Senator Donna Bailey introducing
LD 672, Resolve, to Rename Salmon Falls Bridge in Buxton
the Salmon Falls Veterans Memorial Bridge
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation Tuesday, March 25, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and Esteemed Members of the Joint Standing Committee
Q on Transportation, my name is Donna Bailey, and I proudly represent Senate District 31, which
includes Buxton, Old Orchard Beach, and Saco. Today, I am pleased to introduce my bill
__672, "Resolve, to Rename Salmon Falls Bridge in Buxton the Salmon Falls Veterans Memorial
Bridge." It directs the Department of Transportation to rename Salmon Falls Bridge in Buxton and Hollis the Salmon Falls Veterans Memorial Bridge.
In the days leading up to cloture, the Hon. Ben Chipman, my former Senate colleague who used to be the Chair of this committee, approached me and told me the story of Calista Cross. I'm sure
that many of you are familiar with Calista and her heroic efforts to rename bridges and recognize veterans across Maine. You've likely already worked on several of her bridge renaming bills this
session.
With LD 672,` we have the opportunity to rename another bridge: the Salmon Falls Bridge in
Buxton and Hollis. As the State Senator representing Buxton, I am honored to sponsor this bill. Believe it or not, prior to this year, I had never renamed a bridge. Now, I'm involved with
renaming three: The Captain Christopher S. Cash Memorial Bridge in Old Orchard Beach and Saco, the General Wallace H. Nutting Memorial Bridge in Biddeford and Saco, and -- with your support -- the Salmon Falls Veterans Memorial Bridge in Buxton and Hollis.
I am not sure if Calista will be present today. When I reached out to her, she said that she has to monitor the weather before she considers making the trip to the State House. Regardless, I am
including the letters of support, which Calista worked on, from both Buxton and Hollis to rename the Salmon Falls Bridge.
As lawmakers, we serve on different committees and work on many bills. With this particular one, I am pleased to help honor Maine's veterans. Whether residents or visitors, people who see these bridge names will remember the brave men and women who served in the armed forces. In
this way, we will not forget their patriotism and sacrifice. We can demonstrate our gratitude for
their efforts to protect our freedoms and rights.
l

I thank the Committee for its time, and I would be happy to answer any questions

Testimony of Meghan Russo Maine Department of Transportation
Before the 132"" Legislature, Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Neither For Nor Against
LD 672, Resolve, to Rename the Salmon Falls Bridge Between Buxton and Hollis the
Salmon Falls Veterans Memorial Bridge
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, I am Meghan Russo, Director of Government Affairs at MaineDOT. MaineDOT is neither for nor against LD 672.
MaineDOT considers the naming of bridges, roadways, and other state transportation infrastructure to be within the purview of the Legislature. Simply put, we build them and you name them. Accordingly, we generally do not take positions on so-called "naming bills." However, we usually submit written testimony regarding whether the particular infrastructure under consideration has been named before, and if so what those name(s) are. In this case, we are not aware of any previous legislatively-sanctioned names for this bridge. MaineDOT's
current inventory number for this structure is 3708.
Thank you.
